answer: Agents can sell a sable illustration, assess a relic or map a ledge, but bonuses pay once per epoch per verified human sponsor. A proof-of-personhood issuer allows one credential per person. Each claim must prove in zero knowledge that its nullifier is the hash of a valid credential’s fixed secret, the market ID and the epoch; the contract rejects previously used nullifiers across all accounts. More agent accounts earn nothing extra, so attackers must recruit additional verified humans. This relies on the issuer blocking duplicate credentials and cannot prevent collusion.
